title: Genetic Inheritance Patterns
objectives: Distinguish between Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance
Recognize inheritance patterns in genetic disorders
Apply probability rules to genetic crosses

mendelian_inheritance.title: Classical Inheritance Patterns
mendelian_inheritance.content:
• Autosomal Dominant: Huntington's disease (50% offspring risk)
  • Autosomal Recessive: Cystic fibrosis (25% risk)
  • X-linked: Hemophilia (son of carrier mother has 50% risk)

non_mendelian.title: Complex Inheritance
non_mendelian.content:
Non-Mendelian Mechanisms
• Mitochondrial: Maternal inheritance (e.g., MELAS)
• Imprinting: Prader-Willi/Angelman syndromes
• Mosaicism: Post-zygotic mutations

pedigree_analysis.title: Clinical Interpretation
pedigree_analysis.content:
Pedigree Red Flags

Dominant: Vertical transmission

Recessive: Horizontal pattern, consanguinity

X-linked: No male-to-male transmission

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why can two unaffected parents have a child with an autosomal dominant disorder?

Possible explanations include germline mosaicism in one parent or de novo mutation in the child.
